To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have proposed a multiresonator based chipless RFID circuit that can encode multiple data bits using modified complementary split ring (MCSRR).

we have developed a novel MCSRR based multiresonator for chipless RFID tags that allows encoding of two bits of data using one MCSRR and hence the total number of data bits that can be encoded is increased by 50% as compared to the existing multiresonator designs.
we proposed a novel multiresonator based chipless RFID circuit that can encode 4 bits of data in a compact area and can be used for the implementation of fully printable chipless tag.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a compact chipless tag with enhanced data capacity and bandwidth.
the development of a compact and low cost chipless RFID tag based on spectral signature.
the design and development of a compact chipless UWB tag for spectral signature based identification.
